messages:
maya: Hey folks – noticed noisy oscillation on dedicated-ml-1 over the last ~6h. Autoscaler keeps giving short leases then reclaiming, tenants prewarm, requests spike, we scale up, then scale down within minutes. Cost pinging and latency jitter.

maya: Quick snapshot: autoscaler_scaled_total(dedicated-ml-1) +7 in last 6h, median lease_duration ~90s, but 30% of leases <30s. pool_free_gpus hits 0 -> +3 -> 0 repeatedly.

maya: PromQL I used:```
sum(increase(autoscaler_scaled_total{pool="dedicated-ml-1"}[6h]))
quantile_over_time(0.5, pool_alloc_lease_duration_seconds{pool="dedicated-ml-1"}[6h])
rate(pool_free_gpus{pool="dedicated-ml-1"}[5m])
```

devon: yikes. can you attach the raw logs from the scaler and allocator for the worst 30m window? also which tenants saw latency spikes?

maya: pasted small excerpt:```
[2026-03-19T10:23:01Z] allocator: grant lease tenant=search-team size=2 ttl=60s
[2026-03-19T10:23:58Z] allocator: revoke lease tenant=search-team id=x123 reason=preempt queueshort
[2026-03-19T10:24:05Z] autoscaler: scale_up pool=dedicated-ml-1 delta=2 trigger=headroom
[2026-03-19T10:25:40Z] autoscaler: scale_down pool=dedicated-ml-1 delta=2 idle_timeout=90s
```

liam: looks like two coupled issues: (1) lease TTL + immediate reclaim, (2) admission lacks a backlog-aware backpressure signal. TTL=60s is too short when you have prewarm + jitter.

liam: proposal: switch to "lease heartbeat" model + extend default min_lease=180s, but allow early release. heartbeat extends ttl on active requests. Add metric: pool_lease_heartbeat_last_seconds{pool,tenant}.

liam: second, admission should read pending_queue_length and recent_alloc_rate to decide whether to accept prewarm. Pseudocode:```
avail = total_gpus - reserved_headroom - active_leases
if avail >= req: accept
else if pending_queue_len > backlog_threshold: reject with 429 backpressure
else: trigger prewarm (but mark request as speculative)
```

sara: +1 for heartbeat. tradeoff: longer leases increase cost under low utilization. but early-release path keeps cost bounded. we should add a small hysteresis window to the control loop (eg 120s) to avoid flip-flopping.

sara: we should also expose a new telemetry set: lease_state{pool,tenant} (values: pending|active|releasing), pending_queue_length, speculative_prewarms_active. That will let ops correlate prewarms -> unnecessary scale ups.

maya: good. i also want clearer signals from the autoscaler when it scales for "speculative prewarm" vs "confirmed demand". right now logs just say trigger=headroom. can we add cause=speculative_prewarm or cause=confirmed_request?

ops-bot: [autoscaler] scaled pool=dedicated-ml-1 delta=2 cause=speculative_prewarm at 2026-03-19T10:24:05Z (link: https://ci.internal/scale-events/2921234567) :information_source:

devon: if we add heartbeat, we need to avoid race where heartbeat client fails and kernel keeps the GPU busy. heartbeat must be conservative: if no heartbeat, transition to draining but give a short grace (eg 30s) for transient failures.

liam: agree. implement state machine: ACTIVE -> (missed_heartbeats) -> DRAINING -> RELEASING. DRAINING allows current in-flight requests to finish, scheduler avoids new assignments. metrics record transition counts.

sara: experimental plan:
- instrument telemetry (lease_state, pending_queue_length, speculative_prewarms_active) in allocator (canary on dedicated-ml-1)
- bump min_lease to 180s and add heartbeat extension API (client-side lib + fallback)
- add admission backpressure: reject prewarm if pending_queue_len > 50 or 95th queue latency > 2s
- add 120s hysteresis on autoscaler (don’t scale down within 120s of a scale up)
- run canary 48h, compare scale events and cost delta

maya: +1. owner? devex for client lib + eng-runtime for allocator/autoscaler changes. can we split tasks?

liam: I can own allocator changes (lease_state metrics + heartbeat + state machine). devon can own autoscaler admission changes + hysteresis. sara can own the canary config + dashboards. maya will validate costs and SLA impact.

devon: noted. i'll add an integration test that simulates speculative prewarms + bursts to validate no oscillation. also add a grafana panel: speculative_prewarms_active / total_scale_events.

sara: quick decision note: we accept temporary increased cost on this pool for 48h to reduce jitter and avoid repeated cold-start churn. if cost > +15% we abort.

maya: thanks. can everyone drop short PR owners and ETA in the #eng-releases thread? i'll coordinate rollout windows with infra.

liam: PR: allocator#421 (wip), ETA 5d.

devon: PR: autoscaler#988 (draft), ETA 6d.

sara: dashboard PR: observability#203, canary config PR: infra-config#79, ETA 3d.

maya: great. please include a changelog entry and a runbook snippet for how to abort the canary (rollback flags: autoscaler.spec.canaryMode=false, allocator.feature.lease_heartbeat=false).

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0319-01 linked to thread 2921234567.

maya: end state: instrumentation + heartbeat + admission backpressure + 120s hysteresis canary on dedicated-ml-1 for 48h. I'll follow up with cost analysis after 48h. :white_check_mark:
